result.topic_en: Further notes on the (spherical) pentagon (pentagramma mirificum): relations among the squared tangents α, β, γ, δ, ε of the sides, their dependence, the expression of all of them in terms of two, a numerical example, and the 'beautiful equation' 3+Σα = αβγδε.
result.transcription:
240   III S. 484
Noch über das Fünfeck   (S. 181)

Die Relationen zwischen den Seiten so: [-r=1-] {+r=1+} gesetzt,
Quadrate der
Tangenten | Secanten | Cosecanten . Die Gleichungen
$\alpha$ | $\gamma\delta$ | $\frac{\gamma\delta}{\alpha}$ | $1+\alpha=\gamma\delta$
$\beta$ | $\delta\varepsilon$ | $\frac{\delta\varepsilon}{\beta}$ | $1+\beta=\delta\varepsilon$
$\gamma$ | $\varepsilon\alpha$ | $\frac{\varepsilon\alpha}{\gamma}$ | $1+\gamma=\varepsilon\alpha$
$\delta$ | $\alpha\beta$ | $\frac{\alpha\beta}{\delta}$ | $1+\delta=\alpha\beta$
$\varepsilon$ | $\beta\gamma$ | $\frac{\beta\gamma}{\varepsilon}$ | $1+\varepsilon=\beta\gamma$
Diese Gleichungen [-sind-] sind nicht unabhängig.
Es ist nemlich identisch:
$(1+\gamma)\{1+\beta-\delta\varepsilon\}-(1+\beta)\{1+\gamma-\varepsilon\alpha\} = \varepsilon\{(1+\beta)\alpha-(1+\gamma)\delta\}$
$= \varepsilon\{[\alpha\beta-\delta-1]-[\gamma\delta-\alpha-1]\}$
und auf ähnliche Weise wird die fünfte aus dreien der übrigen abgeleitet. Aus zweien der Größen $\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta,\varepsilon$ folgen die übrigen
$\beta=\frac{1+\alpha+\gamma}{\alpha\gamma}$ | $\beta=\frac{1+\delta}{\alpha}$ | $\gamma=\frac{1+\alpha}{\alpha\beta-1}$ | $\beta=\frac{1+\varepsilon}{\alpha\varepsilon-1}$
$\delta=\frac{1+\alpha}{\gamma}$ | $\gamma=\frac{1+\alpha}{\delta}$ | $\delta=\alpha\beta-1$ | $\gamma=\alpha\varepsilon-1$
$\varepsilon=\frac{1+\gamma}{\alpha}$ | $\varepsilon=\frac{1+\alpha+\delta}{\alpha\delta}$ | $\varepsilon=\frac{1+\beta}{\alpha\beta-1}$ | $\delta=\frac{1+\alpha}{\alpha\varepsilon-1}$

z.B | Cosin$^2$ | Sinus$^2$
$\alpha=9$ | $\frac{1}{10}$ | $\frac{9}{10}$ | 71.33.56
$\beta=\frac{2}{3}$ | $\frac{3}{5}$ | $\frac{2}{5}$ | 39.13.54
$\gamma=2$ | $\frac{1}{3}$ | $\frac{2}{3}$ | 54.44.7
$\delta=5$ | $\frac{1}{6}$ | $\frac{5}{6}$ | 65.54.19
$\varepsilon=\frac{1}{3}$ | $\frac{3}{4}$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ | 30° 0' 0"

Schöne Gleichung
$3+\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\delta+\varepsilon=\alpha\beta\gamma\delta\varepsilon$
$=\frac{(1+\alpha)(1+\beta)(1+\delta)}{\delta}$
[-$=\sqrt{(1+\alpha)(1+\beta)(1+\gamma)(1+\delta)(1+\varepsilon)}$-]

Einfachste[?] Form v. $\frac{(1+\alpha)(1+\beta)\alpha\beta}{\alpha\beta-1} = \frac{1}{\tang f^2 \tang g^2 \cos(f-g)\cos(f+g)}$

methods.what: Relations between squared tangents of the sides of the self-polar spherical pentagon (r=1)
Identity showing the five relations are dependent (fifth follows from three others)
Expression of the remaining quantities from two given ones
Numerical example with squared cosines, sines and angles
Gauss's 'beautiful equation' for the pentagramma mirificum
Simplest form of the product in terms of angles f, g
